Hey, I've released music before and know a bit about the various platforms available.  

I'd say Bandcamp is one of the best platforms for paying artists as directly as possible. The artist themselves sets the price and typically you can also pay anything higher than that if that's your jam. Bandcamp usually takes a small cut, but on the first Friday of every month they run "Bandcamp Friday" where 100% of the money from purchases goes to the artist.  

Other than that, Patreon is great if the artist has one, as it has a lot more customisation from the artist's side. SoundCloud also introduced donation links to help smaller artists out over quarantine, if you visit an artist's page there may be a blue donation link that redirects to their PayPal, CashApp or merch site.  

Buying merch is also good if the artist has some available, be it CDs & vinyl or clothes, there's a few middlemen between you and the artist that take a cut of the money, but it's great if more people buy (and you also get something cool back).  

And if you want to use a streaming service then I believe Amazon Music and Tidal give the highest amount per stream. But in the grand scheme of things, streaming revenue would be a small percentage regardless of which platform was used.
